<subject>Catherine Storey for Corporate Transactions Advisory</subject>
<body>
I talked to each of you a couple of weeks ago, and this topic got pushed aside due to some other pressing issues. However, each of you agreed that a standard cutoff time was acceptable for client matter intake and documentation across our advisory streams.

The best option will be to agree to cutoff at 4pm each day (just to get an idea of the numbers we were talking about, I looked at yesterday to determine how many new instructions were received after 4pm London time. We had three M&A advisory matters, and two Compliance consulting enquiries). After 4pm, the matter management system would automatically assign new Corporate instructions to the following day. However, for those matters that do not close after 4pm, the various practice groups would need to remember that these instructions are the following day's business. I am not sure how the procedures in Finance Operations would need to be modified for the engagement team's time tracking, as the official billing records would not include these late matters. Can Finance Operations run supplemental reports to ensure that the teams have accurate time allocation each morning?

I would appreciate any comments that you may have, and regardless, please re-confirm that a cutoff of 4pm works for each of your respective groups.

Danielle Saunders
Vice President, Meridian Law & Advisory LLP
+44 20 7946 2847
</body>
